title: The MLP
summary: Neurons that fire on specific patterns, and the two-thirds of the weights they hold.

steps.text: After attention, each position passes through an **MLP** on its own: expand to 4× the width, apply GELU, project back. These layers hold about two-thirds of the model's weights.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She

steps.text: This is the expanded layer before the non-linearity: one column per neuron, one row per position.

After **GELU**, negative values are squashed towards zero. Zero is white, positive values are red, and the deeper the red, the larger the value. Columns that stay white for every position are neurons that did not fire on this prompt; a deep red cell is a neuron responding strongly to something at that position. Hover over a cell to see its value and how it compares with the largest value in the map.

ask.question: Click a deep red cell: a neuron firing strongly at one position.
ask.correct: Its provenance shows the pre-activation u and GELU(u). The interventions tab can now ablate exactly this neuron.
ask.hint: Hover over the darkest red cells. The colour scale tops out below the largest value (see the range above the map), so many cells look equally dark. The tooltip shows each cell as a percentage of the largest value: any cell at 50% or more counts.

steps.text: Ablate that neuron (interventions tab, “use L1 neuron … from the inspector”) and watch which predictions change. Most single neurons change little: the work is spread out.
